feedback: Candidate review based only on iteration 0, where all 60 trials ended off_track (progress 0.04 to 0.12, max_error about 0.061 m, one line-loss event per run, low steering_oscillation of 0.06 to 0.07). The candidate is valid: five sensors match five weights, x-positions of ±0.04 are inside the ±0.08 limit, y = 0.03 is in range, and every controller field is within its limit. Its changes address the failure mode seen in iteration 0. Widening the span to ±0.04 m keeps the line visible at larger offsets, which should reduce the line losses that started every failure. Adding ki = 0.3 targets the constant left/right motor-mismatch bias that proportional control alone cannot remove. Raising kd to 0.1 adds damping, and lowering base_speed to 1.4 gives more correction margin. The rationale's claims about performance are hypotheses, not measurements. Nothing has raced for this candidate yet, so do not assume completion. This is the first real test of the wider sensor span and integral term, and the race is needed to see whether either helps. Next review, use the telemetry as follows. If progress is near 1 but completion_time is above 3 s, raise controller.base_speed to about 1.7 and keep the other fields. If line_loss_events is still above 0 with max_error near 0.06, widen the sensor set further (for example x = ±0.06 with weights ±1.5 or add sensors) or change line_loss to search_left or search_right, depending on the side where the line is lost. If the robot drifts steadily with low oscillation, raise ki to 0.5 before changing speed. Change one group of fields per revision so the effect stays readable.
requested_changes: If completion_time is above 3 s with progress near 1, set controller.base_speed to 1.7 and keep the other controller and geometry fields, because iteration 0 shows speed is the constraint once the robot stays on the line.

If line_loss_events stays above 0 with max_error near 0.06, extend the sensor span to x = ±0.06 with weights scaled to about ±1.5 at the outer sensors, or change controller.line_loss to search_left, comparing against iteration 0's one loss per run.
If the robot drifts with low steering_oscillation and max_error still grows over the run, raise controller.ki from 0.3 to 0.5 to remove more of the constant motor-mismatch bias, keeping kp at 3.0.
